heading: INT. ORBITAL GREENHOUSE RING - NIGHT CYCLE

units.text: INT. ORBITAL GREENHOUSE RING - NIGHT CYCLE
Curved rows of tomato vines under violet grow-light.
Condensation beads on the inside of the viewports.
Earth hangs in the glass like a bruised plum.
CAPTAIN ADEOLA NWOSU, fifties, grey at the temples, sits on an upturned crate, peeling an orange with a care that suggests she has no intention of eating it.
Opposite, botanist LEIF ARNARSON, forties, kneels at a tray of seedlings, misting them one by one.
ENGINEER MIRA SOLANKI, thirties, leans on a pipe rack with a wrench she isn't using.
Nobody speaks for a long time.
A pump ticks.
Leif counts leaves under his breath.
Mira, the coolant loop.
units.name: ADEOLA

units.text: Holding.
units.name: MIRA

units.text: Good.
units.name: ADEOLA

units.text: Leif sprays the last seedling and wipes his hands on his trousers, slowly, one finger at a time.
Mira turns the wrench over, sets it on the rack, picks it up again.
Adeola finishes the orange, lays the peel in a single unbroken spiral on her knee, and does not look at either of them.
You'll be fine. You'll all be fine.
units.name: LEIF

units.text: Leif.
units.name: MIRA

units.text: I'm talking to the plants.
units.name: LEIF

units.text: Everyone is fine. Dinner at nineteen hundred.
units.name: ADEOLA

units.text: She stands.
The peel falls.
Mira steps over it without comment.
Leif reaches for it, then stops, hand hovering.
A soft chime from the wall panel.
Amber light slides across all three faces.
Nobody moves toward it.
That's the pressure alert.
units.name: LEIF

units.text: It's been doing that.
units.name: MIRA

units.text: I know.
units.name: ADEOLA

units.text: Mira finally crosses to the panel.
Reads it.
Her thumb presses the screen, once, as if testing for a pulse.
She turns, and her face gives away what she doesn't say.
Leif sees it.
He sits down on the floor between the trays, knees up.
Adeola walks to the viewport, her reflection laid over the Earth.
Eleven days.
units.name: ADEOLA

units.text: Mira picks up the peel from the floor and holds it out to Leif.
He takes it.
They look at each other, and then at the captain's back, and no one asks.
